NOVELTY STATEMENT — STANDARD PRACTICE: Fixed-time filter replacement (90-day schedule) with no adaptive mechanism. NOVEL MECHANISM: Adaptive filter life prediction based on fan power consumption patterns and pressure drop correlation to filter loading state. PHYSICS CONNECTION: Filter loading increases resistance, requiring fan power to maintain airflow; power consumption patterns correlate with loading state, allowing prediction of when resistance will reach a critical threshold.

PHYSICS CHECK — GOVERNING RELATION: ΔP = k × v^n (pressure drop proportional to velocity^n, where n≈1.5-2 for loaded filters). FAN POWER: P_fan ∝ ΔP × Q (power proportional to pressure drop times flow rate). MAGNITUDE VERIFICATION: A 50% increase in pressure drop typically increases fan power by 30-50%, which is detectable above normal operational noise in BMS data.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — COMPONENTS/MATERIALS:
- BMS data acquisition system (existing, same class as standard practice)
- Supply fan power sensor (existing, same class as standard practice)
- Return fan power sensor (existing, same class as standard practice)
- Differential pressure sensor across filter bank (if not available, same class as standard practice's maintenance instrumentation)
- Outdoor airflow sensor (existing, same class as standard practice)
- Occupancy schedule data (existing, same class as standard practice)
- Processing algorithm (software implementation, same class as standard practice's BMS monitoring capabilities)

ASSUMPTION: The BMS has sufficient data logging frequency (at least hourly) to capture power consumption patterns. Justification: Standard practice requires regular maintenance checks, which implies existing monitoring capability.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- INSTALLABILITY: SAME - uses existing BMS infrastructure, no new physical installation required
- OPERABILITY: SAME - operates within existing BMS framework, no additional operator training needed beyond standard BMS monitoring
- MAINTENANCE: SAME - no additional maintenance requirements beyond standard BMS maintenance
- COST CLASS: SAME - leverages existing sensors and BMS capabilities, only requires software implementation
- CONCLUSION: Same burden class as fixed-time replacement, but with adaptive capability

EXECUTABLE TEST — PROTOCOL:
1. Install data collection system to record all BMS points for 6 months on identical air-handling units
2. Implement the predictor algorithm on test units while maintaining fixed replacement on control units
3. Record actual filter replacement events and predicted replacement events
4. Measure unnecessary replacements (replacements before filter actually needed)

INSTRUMENTS:
- BMS data logging system
- Differential pressure gauge (for validation)
- Airflow measurement device (for validation)

PASS/FAIL THRESHOLDS:
- PASS: Predictor correctly identifies filter replacement need within 1 week of actual need, with <20% false positives (unnecessary replacements)
- FAIL: Predictor fails to identify replacement need within 1 week, or has >20% false positives

DURATION: 6 months of continuous operation across multiple seasons

KILL CRITERION: If at any point the predictor causes a filter to overload (pressure drop exceeds design limits by 15%), the test fails immediately.
